verses.text: There is naturally in every man a desire to know, but what profiteth knowledge without the fear of God?
verses.modernizedText: There is naturally in every person a desire to know, but what good is knowledge without the fear of God?

verses.text: Better of a surety is a lowly peasant who serveth God, than a proud philosopher who watcheth the stars and neglecteth the knowledge of himself.
verses.modernizedText: Certainly a humble peasant who serves God is better than a proud philosopher who watches the stars and neglects knowledge of himself.

verses.text: He who knoweth himself well is vile in his own sight; neither regardeth he the praises of men.
verses.modernizedText: The person who knows himself well is vile in his own sight; he pays no regard to the praises of others.

verses.text: If I knew all the things that are in the world, and were not in charity, what should it help me before God, who is to judge me according to my deeds?
verses.modernizedText: If I knew everything in the world and had no charity, how would it help me before God, who will judge me according to my deeds?

verses.text: Rest from inordinate desire of knowledge, for therein is found much distraction and deceit.
verses.modernizedText: Rest from an excessive desire for knowledge, for in it there is much distraction and deceit.

verses.text: Those who have knowledge desire to appear learned, and to be called wise.
verses.modernizedText: Those who have knowledge desire to appear learned and to be called wise.

verses.text: Many things there are to know which profiteth little or nothing to the soul.
verses.modernizedText: There are many things to know that benefit the soul little or not at all.

verses.text: And foolish out of measure is he who attendeth upon other things rather than those which serve to his soul’s health.
verses.modernizedText: And anyone who attends to other things rather than those that serve the health of his soul is exceedingly foolish.

verses.text: Many words satisfy not the soul, but a good life refresheth the mind, and a pure conscience giveth great confidence towards God.
verses.modernizedText: Many words do not satisfy the soul, but a good life refreshes the mind, and a pure conscience gives great confidence before God.

verses.text: The greater and more complete thy knowledge, the more severely shalt thou be judged, unless thou hast lived holily.
verses.modernizedText: The greater and more complete your knowledge, the more severely you will be judged, unless you have lived a holy life.

verses.text: Therefore be not lifted up by any skill or knowledge that thou hast; but rather fear concerning the knowledge which is given to thee.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, do not be lifted up by any skill or knowledge you have; instead, fear because of the knowledge that has been given to you.

verses.text: If it seemeth to thee that thou knowest many things, and understandest them well, know also that there are many more things which thou knowest not.
verses.modernizedText: If it seems to you that you know many things and understand them well, know also that there are many more things you do not know.

verses.text: Be not high-minded, but rather confess thine ignorance.
verses.modernizedText: Do not be proud, but instead confess your ignorance.

verses.text: Why desirest thou to lift thyself above another, when there are found many more learned and more skilled in the Scripture than thou?
verses.modernizedText: Why do you desire to lift yourself above another when many are more learned and more skilled in Scripture than you?

verses.text: If thou wilt know and learn anything with profit, love to be thyself unknown and to be counted for nothing.
verses.modernizedText: If you want to know and learn anything to your benefit, love to be unknown and counted as nothing.

verses.text: That is the highest and most profitable lesson, when a man truly knoweth and judgeth lowly of himself.
verses.modernizedText: This is the highest and most profitable lesson: for a person truly to know himself and think humbly of himself.

verses.text: To account nothing of one’s self, and to think always kindly and highly of others, this is great and perfect wisdom.
verses.modernizedText: To think nothing of oneself and always to think kindly and highly of others is great and perfect wisdom.

verses.text: Even shouldest thou see thy neighbor sin openly or grievously, yet thou oughtest not to reckon thyself better than he, for thou knowest not how long thou shalt keep thine integrity.
verses.modernizedText: Even if you see your neighbor sin openly or grievously, you should not consider yourself better than he, for you do not know how long you will keep your integrity.

verses.text: All of us are weak and frail; hold thou no man more frail than thyself.
verses.modernizedText: All of us are weak and frail; consider no one more frail than yourself.
